The pages give the date, not a boundary: the region is Cliopatria's 1516 shape. Repair 2026-11-01 (fx-20): the region no longer holds the Low Countries (Habsburg Netherlands page: in 1516 Charles 'continued to rule over his domains in the Netherlands and Burgundy' 'without annexation'); the Franche-Comte comes by ledger/1.

region.text: the Free County of Burgundy (Franche-Comte), Charles's as count and drawn with Spain from March 1516

ledger.note: March 1516: the Free County of Burgundy (Franche-Comte) is drawn with the new state, as the one holder of the county until a dossier of its own exists (the habsburg-netherlands notes ask for 'franche-comte', Habsburg Franche-Comte 1493-1678). Free County of Burgundy page: the county went to Philip at Senlis in 1493; in 1512 it was 'included into the newly formed Burgundian Circle and administered as part of the Habsburg Netherlands'; Charles succeeded Philip and became King of Spain in 1516. The same page says the county 'was never annexed into the Kingdom of Spain' and 'remained a domain within the Holy Roman Empire', and the Spanish Netherlands page calls it a separate possession, not part of the Spanish Netherlands, under Habsburg rule from 1493. So this is a drawing convention, confidence 1: this dossier's shapes carry the county to 1678 (wars/5, wars/6) and the Cliopatria Habsburg Monarchy row (habsburg-monarchy), the previous counterpart, no longer draws it from 1516. Replaces the earlier reading of this event, a gain of the Low Countries and the Franche-Comte from habsburg-netherlands: Habsburg Netherlands page: 'In 1516, Charles became the king of Spain, but also continued to rule over his domains in the Netherlands and Burgundy'; the Low Countries came to the Spanish Crown only in 1556 ('Philip II of Spain, Charles' son, inherited the Seventeen Provinces and incorporated them into the Spanish Crown'). Repair 2026-11-01 (fx-20).

region.text: Catalonia and Roussillon

ledger.note: 1640: Catalonia rises against Philip IV. region.text: the Kingdom of Spain as Cliopatria draws it from 1640, with Ceuta, which 'chose to remain under Spanish authority after 1640'

ledger.note: 1 December 1640: the Iberian Union breaks and Spain emerges from it again. The Iberian Union page: 'a revolution by the nobility and high bourgeoisie on 1 December 1640' (infobox 'Portuguese Restoration War: 1 December 1640'); 'Spain recognized Portugal's sovereignty and made peace on 13 February 1668'. After the merge of 1580 this dossier holds no land; the split of Portugal itself belongs to the iberian-union and kingdom-of-portugal dossiers, and here the event gives the kingdom its land back. region.text: Roussillon: 'Perpignan was taken from the Spanish after a siege of 10 months' and 'the whole of Roussillon was under French control'

ledger.note: 1642: France takes Roussillon from the Spanish side, as the kingdom-of-france dossier records (ledger/105, occupation_start 1642). region.text: the frontier lands that stayed in dispute: Zeelandic Flanders, North Brabant and Maastricht

ledger.note: 30 January 1648: the Peace of Munster ends the war with the Dutch. The Habsburg Spain page: Spain 'recognized the independent United Provinces in the Peace of Westphalia'.

region.text: Zeelandic Flanders, North Brabant and Maastricht

ledger.note: 30 January 1648: Spain gives up Zeelandic Flanders, North Brabant and Maastricht to the Dutch Republic in the Peace of Munster. Cliopatria drops North Brabant already in 1640; the page's 1648 is the legal transfer.

region.text: Catalonia: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and Tarragona

ledger.note: 1652: Barcelona falls and Catalonia returns to Spain. 'the Spanish offensive was able to capture Barcelona in 1652 after a year of siege. region.text: the County of Roussillon and the northern half of the County of Cerdanya (Cerdanya is not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees gives Roussillon to France. The Franco-Spanish War page dates the treaty 7 November 1659 (infobox) and 5 November (text).

region.text: Roussillon, ceded to France

ledger.note: November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees (7 November in the infobox, 5 November in the text) turns France's hold on Roussillon into a cession (the loss above). Mirrors kingdom-of-france ledger/111. Repair 2026-10-25.

region.text: Artois and the places of Flanders and Hainaut ceded in 1659

ledger.note: November 1659: Artois and a strip of Flanders and Hainaut go to France. 'By the Treaty of the Pyrenees of 1659 the French annexed most of Artois.' The Franco-Spanish War page: France gained Artois, Hainaut and Roussillon. Cliopatria removes Artois already in 1640 (the page does not explain that); the Nord loss of 11 cells shows in the 1659 shape. The region reading of Hainaut is mine.

region.text: the frontier of the Spanish Netherlands: Hainaut, Flanders and the Nord

Mirrors kingdom-of-france ledger/115. Repair 2026-10-25.

region.text: the Free County of Burgundy: Conde 'entered Franche-Comte on 4 February' 1668

ledger.note: February 1668: France overruns Franche-Comte: Conde 'entered Franche-Comte on 4 February'; Besancon and Salins-les-Bains surrendered on 7 February, Dole on 14 February and Gray on 19 February. Mirrors kingdom-of-france ledger/118. Repair 2026-10-25.

region.text: Franche-Comte, returned

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 'signed by Spain and France on 2 May': 'France withdrew from Franche-Comte and the Spanish Netherlands' except eleven towns. Mirrors kingdom-of-france ledger/119. Repair 2026-10-25.

region.text: the frontier of the Spanish Netherlands: Hainaut, Flanders and the Nord

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of Devolution. Mirrors kingdom-of-france ledger/120. Repair 2026-10-25.

region.text: Nord and Hainaut cells lost in the 1670 shape

region.text: Franche-Comte: 'The French invaded in the spring of 1674' and 'overran the whole province in less than six weeks'

region.text: Franche-Comte, ceded to France

region.text: Charleroi and Ath, which Spain 'regains' at Nijmegen

region.text: the Duchy of Milan

region.text: Sicily

ledger.note: August 1717: Spain lands on Sardinia. 'In August 1717, Spanish forces landed on Sardinia'; it was under Spanish control by November 1717. The island belonged to the Emperor under the Utrecht settlement.

region.text: Sicily, invaded in 1718

ledger.note: July 1718: Spain lands on Sicily. 'in July 1718 the Spanish landed 30,000 men on Sicily'; the Cape Passaro defeat followed on 11 August 1718. Sicily belonged to Savoy under the Utrecht settlement.

region.text: Sardinia

ledger.note: 17 February 1720: the Treaty of The Hague returns Sardinia. Philip had to 'relinquish all territory captured in the war'; Savoy received Sardinia, Austria Sicily. The page gives no evacuation date, so the treaty date stands for the end.

region.text: Sicily

ledger.note: 17 February 1720: the Treaty of The Hague returns Sicily (to Austria in an exchange: Victor Amadeus 'was forced to exchange Sicily for that of the less important Kingdom of Sardinia').

region.text: Menorca, ceded with Gibraltar in Article X of the Anglo-Spanish treaty

region.text: Gipuzkoa, where the French took Hondarribia and San Sebastian

region.text: Figueres and Roses in Girona province

region.text: Gipuzkoa, where the French took Hondarribia and San Sebastian

region.text: Figueres and Roses in Girona province

region.text: Menorca, ceded with Gibraltar in Article X of the Anglo-Spanish treaty

region.text: Menorca, ceded with Gibraltar in Article X of the Anglo-Spanish treaty

ledger.note: 1802: the Treaty of Amiens 'called for the return of Menorca to Spain'; Richard Bickerton oversaw the British evacuation. The page gives no month. Repair 2026-10-25.

region.text: the Spain the French held

SCOPE. This dossier is the Cliopatria row 'Kingdom of Spain' (1516-1581, 1640-1872, 1877-1931, 1976-2024) as one continuing state. Cliopatria switches rows at four points and this row has no shape in those years: 1582-1639 Iberian Union (iberian-union), 1873-1876 First Spanish Republic (first-spanish-republic), 1932-1938 Second Spanish Republic and Spanish Nationalists, 1939-1975 Francoist Spain. The ledger hands the land over with merge/split/loss/gain events (1580 and 1640, 1873 and 1875, 1931 and 1975); the receiving dossiers should name this slug as predecessor/successor. Whether the Republics and Franco's state are the same state as the monarchy is a naming choice for the colour agent; this dossier keeps the monarchy.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS THAT ARE WRONG OR SWAPPED (all in keyframe_review).
(1) 1529-1555 (shapes 1529, 1534, 1540, 1547): the Spain shape holds Austria, Bohemia, Silesia, Slovenia, Croatia, Tyrol and (from 1540) Slovakia and western Hungary, which were Ferdinand's, while the Habsburg Monarchy row holds the Low Countries and Franche-Comte; the two rows are swapped until 1556. Corrected: Spain, the Italian kingdoms, Milan from 1535, Roussillon, plus the Low Countries and Franche-Comte.
